title: Direct Integral Decomposition and Type I Groups

items.title: Direct integrals of unitary representations
items.statement: Assume AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let G be a locally compact Hausdorff group and (X,𝔅,μ) a sigma-finite standard-Borel measure space ([[def-standard-borel-space]], [[def-finite-sigma-finite-and-semifinite-measures]]), with a measurable complex Hilbert field having a countable fundamental family ([[def-measurable-hilbert-field-from-a-countable-fundamental-family]]). A measurable field of unitary representations is a family (π_x) such that every π_x is strongly continuous ([[def-strongly-continuous-unitary-representation]]) and x↦π_x(g) is weakly measurable for each fixed g ([[def-measurable-and-decomposable-operator-fields]]); the group identities hold for every x and every g,h. The decomposable operators π(g)=∫_X^⊕π_x(g)dμ(x) ([[thm-measurable-essentially-bounded-operator-fields-act-decomposably]]) define a group homomorphism G→U(𝓗), written π=∫_X^⊕π_xdμ(x) on the direct-integral Hilbert space ([[def-direct-integral-of-a-measurable-hilbert-field]], [[thm-direct-integrals-of-measurable-hilbert-fields-are-hilbert-spaces]]). This construction establishes unitarity and the group law; strong continuity of the integrated action is not asserted here. Changing the field on a μ-null set does not change any induced operator.
items.strategy: For each fixed g, the fibre operators are unitary, so their weakly measurable field is essentially bounded by 1 and defines a decomposable operator. The decomposable-operator theorem preserves adjoints and products. The pointwise identities at every x therefore give π(g)π(h)=π(gh), π(e)=I, and π(g)*=π(g^{-1}); hence every π(g) is unitary. The same theorem identifies fields equal off a null set. Pointwise fibre identities avoid any uncountable intersection of conull sets. Strong continuity is deferred to its separately assigned lemma.
items.axiom_use: AC is inherited through the direct-integral Hilbert-space supplier for completeness and through the decomposable-operator supplier for Hilbert adjoints. This definition makes no arbitrary field or conull-set choices.

items.title: Factor (primary) representations
items.statement: Assume AC. Let G be a topological group and (π,H) a strongly continuous unitary representation on a nonzero Hilbert space. Set M:=π(G)″⊂B(H), the concrete double commutant, and Z(M):=M∩M′. The representation π is factorial, or primary, when Z(M)=C I_H; it is a factor representation when M is a factor. The commutants satisfy π(G)′=(π(G)″)′ by a direct consequence of their definitions. Irreducibility implies factoriality by Schur’s lemma. The converse fails: for every nontrivial ICC discrete group Γ, its left regular representation is factorial but not irreducible; a complete local argument is included in the item.
items.strategy: First realize ℓ²(Γ) as a Hilbert space by identifying it isometrically with L² of counting measure. For S=π(G), show S is *-closed, S'' is a concrete von Neumann algebra, and (S'')'=S'. Schur's lemma gives irreducible ⇒ M' is scalar ⇒ the center is scalar. For every nontrivial ICC discrete Γ, left and right translations show that a central z sends δ_e to a square-summable conjugacy-invariant vector, so z is scalar; a nonidentity right translation is a nonscalar commutant element, so λ is not irreducible. The finitary symmetric group on ℕ gives a concrete ICC witness. AC supplies adjoints, Schur's lemma, and L² completeness; the remaining group and conjugacy calculations use no further choice.

items.title: L1 of a second-countable locally compact group is separable
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $G$ be a second-countable locally compact Hausdorff group with a fixed left Haar measure $\mu$ ([[def-second-countable-space]], [[def-left-haar-integral-and-left-haar-measure]], [[def-complex-haar-lp-spaces-and-compactly-supported-functions]]). Then $L^1(G,\mu;\mathbb C)$ is a separable Banach space. There is a countable Borel algebra $\mathcal A_0$ generating the Borel sigma-algebra of $G$ such that the $\mathbb Q(i)$-linear span of $\{\mathbf 1_A:A\in\mathcal A_0,\ \mu(A)<\infty\}$ is dense in $L^1(G)$. Moreover, the image of $C_c(G;\mathbb C)$ in $L^1(G)$ contains a countable dense subset.
items.strategy: Use a countable relatively compact cover and compact exhaustion. Form specifically the finite-Boolean algebra of the Borel generators; its increasing finite-prefix algebras give countability under Countable Choice. Approximate Cc functions by finite-measure algebra cells and rational-complex values. Earlier finite-powers and countable-union results make the finite coefficient/set lists countable, and AC implies Countable Choice for selecting Cc approximants.

items.axiom_use: Assume AC. The implication AC to DC to Countable Choice is used explicitly: Countable Choice supplies the Lindelof subcover, countability of the generated algebra and countable unions, and the final countable selection from Cc; the published L1-completeness and Cc-density supplier also states AC as a hypothesis. The local compact-cover witnesses, cell points and rational approximants require only finite choice. Step 4 defines its cover as the family of all qualifying base sets, so it makes no choice of neighborhoods indexed by all points of the compact set. No other use of choice is made.

items.title: Measurable fields of von Neumann algebras and their direct integrals
items.statement: Assume AC. Let (X,B,mu) be a sigma-finite standard-Borel measure space and (H_x,e_n(x)) a measurable complex Hilbert field with countable fundamental family. For every x let M_x be a unital concrete von Neumann algebra. The field is measurable if a sequence of weakly measurable operator fields generates M_x for almost every x. Define its direct integral as the set of induced decomposable operators from weakly measurable essentially bounded fields T_x in M_x almost everywhere. Define the diagonal algebra D from L-infinity scalar fields. The item proves D is a unital star-algebra included in the direct-integral set; it makes no weak-operator closure claim.
items.strategy: Use the direct-integral Hilbert theorem and the decomposable-operator theorem to interpret the set as bounded operators. For f in L-infinity, the scalar field f(x)I_Hx has measurable fundamental coefficients, is essentially bounded, and lies in each unital M_x, including zero fibres. Its induced action is M_f. Pointwise operations and the direct-integral pairing show D is a unital star-algebra, and changing f on a null set changes no operator.

references.locator: Chapter 1, §1.I, Definition 1.I.1 (measurable fields) and Definition 1.I.4 with Example 1.I.5 (direct integral and diagonal algebra), printed pp. 69–70

No field or generating family is selected by this definition; the diagonal proof chooses one representative of one L-infinity class at a time.

items.title: Measurable Gram-Schmidt and constant-field trivializations on dimension strata
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $(X,\mathcal B,\mu)$ be a sigma-finite standard-Borel measure space and let $(H_x,e_n(x))_{x\in X}$ be a measurable complex Hilbert field with countable fundamental family. Then: (1) there are measurable sections $f_n$ such that for every $x$ the nonzero $f_n(x)$ form a complete orthonormal system in $H_x$, and $x\mapsto\langle\xi(x),f_n(x)\rangle$ is Borel for every measurable section $\xi$; (2) for each $p\in\{1,2,\ldots\}\cup\{\infty\}$, the dimension stratum $X_p:=\{x:\dim H_x=p\}$ is Borel, and for every fixed separable Hilbert space $K_p$ of dimension $p$ there are unitaries $U_x:H_x\to K_p$ on $X_p$ such that $\xi$ is a measurable section on $X_p$ if and only if $x\mapsto U_x\xi(x)$ is a Borel map; explicitly, $U_x\xi$ has coordinates $\langle\xi(x),f_n(x)\rangle$ after deleting zero frame vectors; (3) weakly measurable operator fields have Borel transported matrix coefficients on each $X_p$, and uniformly bounded transported fields are Borel maps into their weak-operator-topology balls; (4) for every countable family of measurable sections $\xi_k$, the pointwise closed spans $S_x:=\overline{\operatorname{span}}\{\xi_k(x):k\in\mathbb N\}$ form a measurable closed Hilbert subfield, and its direct integral is the closed linear span in $\int_X^\oplus H_x\,d\mu(x)$ of all square-integrable localizations $f\mathbf1_E\xi_k$, where $E=D_j\cap\{x:\|\xi_k(x)\|\le r\}$, $(D_j)$ is any countable finite-measure cover of $X$, $r\in\mathbb R$ with $r\ge1$, and $f$ is any bounded Borel scalar function supported in $E$. The zero-dimensional stratum is Borel as the complement of the positive and infinite-dimensional strata.
items.strategy: Apply measurable fibrewise Gram–Schmidt to the fundamental family and to the given sections. Count active frame vectors to obtain Borel dimension strata. On each stratum, map the active measurable frame to an enumerated orthonormal basis of a fixed separable Hilbert space; use a corrected countable rational-ball basis argument to prove the section criterion. For a countable family of sections, localize on finite-measure sets and bounded-norm pieces, test orthogonality with bounded Borel phases, and use the double-orthogonal-complement theorem to identify the closed span of the localizations with the direct integral of the pointwise closed spans. Real truncation radii reduce to integer radii by Archimedean cofinality. Finally express weak-operator coefficients in the transported bases and prove the WOT topology on each bounded ball is generated by its countable matrix coefficients.

The direct-integral Hilbert theorem uses AC to select representatives of a countable summable subsequence and for its standard-Borel coding and countable generating-algebra argument; it also uses AC for the Countable Choice premise of Parseval. items.title: Closed witness codings and completion measurability of Borel projections
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $X$ and $Y$ be standard Borel spaces with Polish presentations ([[def-standard-borel-space]], [[def-polish-space]]), and use their finite-product standard Borel structure ([[lem-finite-products-of-standard-borel-spaces-are-standard-borel]]). Every Borel relation $R\subseteq X\times Y$ is the projection onto $X\times Y$ of a closed set $F\subseteq X\times Y\times\mathbb N^{\mathbb N}$. If $\mu$ is a sigma-finite Borel measure on $X$, then the projection onto $X$ of every Borel subset of $X\times Y$ is measurable in the completion of $\mu$ and differs from a Borel subset only inside a Borel $\mu$-null set. More generally, if $(A_s)_{s\in\mathbb N^{<\mathbb N}}$ is a decreasing Borel scheme on $X$, meaning $A_t\subseteq A_s$ whenever $s$ is an initial segment of $t$, then its branch union $\bigcup_{f\in\mathbb N^{\mathbb N}}\bigcap_n A_{f|n}$ has the same completion-measurability and Borel-version property. No global Borel selector is asserted.
items.strategy: Use earlier finite-power and AC countable-union suppliers to enumerate finite words, with least-preimage injective indices. Prove Baire Polish coding and countable-product coordinate pairing locally; prove finite Polish products locally. Add closed-subspace completeness/separability and admissible-only nested-ball continuous parametrization of every nonempty Polish space. The existing closed-witness and measured-envelope/Souslin branch arguments then prove the full unchanged Statement.

items.axiom_use: AC is explicit. Its local uses are countable selections: one witness for each set in a closed-coded intersection, an approximating Borel superset at each positive integer, one Borel envelope for each finite-sequence node, and one approximating point-pair for each stage of a closed-projection limit. AC implies Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]), which is also assumed by the measure-completion suppliers. The least-child branch uses the well-order of the naturals and recursion; fixed candidate-pair indices and coordinate pairings use no choice. Countable Choice also supplies the finite-word enumeration and a point from each nonempty basic open intersection in a closed subspace. Baire parametrization uses the least admissible child recursion and no branch-indexed choice. No uncountable family is selected locally.

items.title: Measurable dense selections for fields of nonempty compact sets
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $(X,\mathcal A,\mu)$ be a standard Borel space with a sigma-finite measure ([[def-standard-borel-space]], [[def-measure-space]], [[def-finite-sigma-finite-and-semifinite-measures]]). Let $(K,d)$ be a nonempty compact metric space ([[def-compact-space]], [[def-topological-space]], [[def-metric-space]], [[def-metric-topology]]) with a fixed dense sequence $(k_m)_{m\in\mathbb N}$, and give $K$ its Borel sigma-algebra ([[def-borel-sigma-algebra]]). Suppose $g:X\times K\to[0,\infty)$ has measurable sections $x\mapsto g(x,k)$ for each fixed $k$, continuous sections $k\mapsto g(x,k)$ for each fixed $x$, and nonempty zero sets $C_x:=\{k\in K:g(x,k)=0\}$ for every $x$. Then: (1) there is a sequence of measurable maps $s_j:X\to K$ such that $s_j(x)\in C_x$ for all $x,j$ and $(s_j(x))_{j\in\mathbb N}$ is dense in $C_x$ for every $x$; (2) for every $k\in K$, the function $x\mapsto d(k,C_x):=\inf_{c\in C_x}d(k,c)$ is measurable; and (3) for every open $U\subseteq K$, the hit set $\{x:C_x\cap U\ne\varnothing\}$ is measurable.
items.strategy: Prove measurability of closed-target hit sets by coding proximity and small function values on the fixed countable dense sequence. This gives measurable open hits and measurable distance functions. Recursively select the least dense-sequence point near each current zero fiber and intersect with a small closed ball; compactness yields a unique limit, whose measurability follows from a countable closed-ball criterion. Adding a nonnegative distance penalty restricts the zero set to each small ball, and the resulting countable family of measurable point selections is dense in every fiber.

references.title: Bachir Bekka and Pierre de la Harpe, Unitary Representations of Groups, Duals, and Characters (arXiv:1912.07262v1, 16 December 2019; author-hosted complete book draft)
references.locator: Appendix A.C, Theorem A.C.6, printed p. 409 (PDF p. 408): for a Borel relation with everywhere-surjective projection and a standard Borel measure, it gives a Borel selector on a conull Borel subset and refers its proof to Mackey-76, Theorem Z.2, Chapter 2, §2.2. This is comparison only; the local nested-set argument here gives selectors for every x in the compact zero-set setting.

items.axiom_use: AC is retained as the scaffold's explicit hypothesis, but the proof is choice-free. The fixed dense sequence is input data, recursive indices are least natural numbers, and each point selected as a limit is unique. The sigma-finite measure is also an inherited input and is not used by these Borel conclusions.

items.title: The double commutant theorem for concrete von Neumann algebras
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $H$ be a complex Hilbert space and let $M\subseteq\mathcal B(H)$ be a unital $*$-subalgebra closed in the weak operator topology. Then $M''=M$, and $M$ is also closed in the strong operator topology. Consequently the concrete von Neumann algebras of [[def-von-neumann-algebra-and-commutant]] are exactly the unital $*$-subalgebras that are closed in either of these topologies. For an arbitrary set $\mathcal S\subseteq\mathcal B(H)$ one has $W^*(\mathcal S)''=W^*(\mathcal S)$.
items.strategy: For a unital *-subalgebra A, use its diagonal action on a finite direct sum H^n. The closed orbit span of a tuple is reducing; its projection commutes with the diagonal action, and the projection blocks lie in A'. Thus every T in A'' sends each finite tuple into the orbit closure and is SOT-approximable. This proves the WOT/SOT closure equivalence and the bicommutant identity. Apply the same approximation to the unital *-algebra generated by S and compare its WOT closure with the WOT-closed bicommutant.
items.axiom_use: Assume AC. AC implies Countable Choice by thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice. Countable Choice is the exact premise for the closed-subspace orthogonal decomposition and Hilbert-adjoint suppliers, and hence for the orthogonal projection used in the finite-block argument. The concrete von Neumann algebra and general direct-sum interfaces also state AC. Their finite instances, and the individual approximant chosen for a fixed tuple and tolerance, require no further choice.

items.title: States, tracial states and faithful normal traces on a von Neumann algebra
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $M\subseteq\mathcal B(H)$ be a concrete von Neumann algebra on a complex Hilbert space $H$ ([[def-von-neumann-algebra-and-commutant]], [[def-space-of-bounded-linear-operators]]). A complex-linear functional $\tau:M\to\mathbb C$ is **positive** if $\tau(P)\in[0,+\infty)$ for every positive operator $P\in M$ ([[def-self-adjoint-positive-unitary-and-normal-operator]]), a **state** if it is positive and $\tau(I_H)=1$, **normal** if its restriction to the operator-norm unit ball of $M$ is continuous for the relative weak-operator topology ([[def-strong-and-weak-operator-topologies]], [[def-operator-norm]]), **tracial** if $\tau(ST)=\tau(TS)$ for all $S,T\in M$, and **faithful** if $\tau(T^*T)=0$ implies $T=0$. A **faithful normal tracial state** is a positive normalized trace that is both normal and faithful. In particular, $(M,\tau)$ is a **finite tracial von Neumann algebra** when $\tau$ is a faithful normal tracial state. If $H=\{0\}$ then $M=\{0\}$ and has no state, since $I_H=0$.

For a nonzero finite-dimensional complex Hilbert space $K$, the normalized matrix trace $\operatorname{tr}_K/\dim K$ is a faithful normal tracial state on $\mathcal B(K)$, and it is the unique tracial state.

For a discrete group $\Gamma$ equipped with the discrete topology, let $H_\Gamma=\ell^2(\Gamma,\mathbb C)$, whose Hilbert-space structure under AC is established in the proof. Define the left and right regular operators by
$$
(\lambda_\Gamma(g)f)(h)=f(g^{-1}h),\qquad (\rho_\Gamma(g)f)(h)=f(hg)\qquad(g,h\in\Gamma).
$$
Put $L(\Gamma):=W^*(\lambda_\Gamma(\Gamma))$ using the concrete generated von Neumann algebra of [[def-von-neumann-algebra-and-commutant]]. Then
$$
\tau_\Gamma(T):=\langle T\delta_e,\delta_e\rangle\qquad(T\in L(\Gamma))
$$
is a faithful normal tracial state on $L(\Gamma)$.
items.strategy: Retain the complete local normalized matrix trace and discrete group trace verification. Use the earlier proved AC implies DC implies Countable Choice theorem for the L2 Hilbert-space premise. Positivity, WOT normality, right-regular faithfulness and separate-WOT extension of traciality are unchanged.

items.title: Commensurator, unitary characters and monomial induced representations in the transversal model
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let G be a topological group and H≤G an open subgroup. (1) The commensurator Comm_G(H) consists of those g for which H∩g^{-1}Hg has finite index in both subgroups; it is a subgroup containing H. (2) A unitary character is a continuous homomorphism χ:H→T. (3) For a right transversal T with G=⊔_{t∈T}Ht and e∈T, write tg=α(t,g)(t·g) uniquely with α(t,g)∈H and t·g∈T. The formula (π(g)f)(t)=χ(α(t,g))f(t·g) defines the monomial induced representation on ℓ²(T); it is strongly continuous and δ_e is cyclic. If G is locally compact, this model is unitarily equivalent to the quotient covariant-function model and hence to standard unitary induction. If G is second-countable, T can be chosen countable and the representation is separable.
items.strategy: The transversal is selected using AC. Commensurability is a conjugation-invariant equivalence relation, so the usual composition and inverse calculations show Comm_G(H) is a subgroup. Uniqueness of the decomposition tg=α(t,g)(t·g) gives the right action and cocycle identities; these prove the representation law, and the right action permutes T while |χ|=1, proving unitarity. Openness of H and continuity of χ prove strong continuity on each basis vector near the identity; density of finite-support vectors and unitarity extend it to all vectors. The identity π(t^{-1})δ_e=δ_t proves cyclicity. For locally compact G, inversion identifies left cosets Ht with right cosets t^{-1}H; evaluation F↦(t↦F(t^{-1})) intertwines the covariant model with this formula after normalizing the discrete quotient measure to counting measure.

items.title: C star state GNS construction, purity and Polish pure-state spaces
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $A$ be a complex C*-algebra and let $\phi$ be a state, meaning a positive bounded linear functional of norm one ([[def-c-star-algebra]], [[def-state-on-a-c-star-algebra]]). There is a Hilbert space $H_\phi$, a bounded *-representation $\pi_\phi:A\to\mathcal B(H_\phi)$ ([[def-space-of-bounded-linear-operators]], [[def-hilbert-space-adjoint]]), and a unit vector $\xi_\phi$ such that $\overline{\pi_\phi(A)\xi_\phi}=H_\phi$ and $\phi(a)=\langle\pi_\phi(a)\xi_\phi,\xi_\phi\rangle$ for every $a\in A$. This representation is nondegenerate, and any two such triples are related by a unique unitary intertwiner taking one cyclic vector to the other. If $A$ is separable, then $H_\phi$ is separable. A state is **pure** when it is an extreme point of the convex state space; a representation is **irreducible** when it has no closed invariant subspaces other than $\{0\}$ and its whole Hilbert space. The GNS representation is irreducible exactly when $\phi$ is pure.

Write $\pi_\phi(A)'$ for the bounded operators commuting with every $\pi_\phi(a)$. The assignment $T\mapsto\psi_T$, $\psi_T(a)=\langle\pi_\phi(a)T\xi_\phi,\xi_\phi\rangle$, is an order isomorphism from $\{T\in\pi_\phi(A)':0\le T\le I\}$ onto the bounded positive functionals $\psi$ satisfying $0\le\psi\le\phi$.

For separable $A$, the pure-state space with its weak-star topology is Polish. If $A$ is unital, its state space is weak-star compact and its pure states are exactly the extreme points; if $A$ is also separable, that state space is metrizable. If $A$ is nonunital, pure states correspond by restriction and unique state extension to the pure states of the minimal unitization other than its augmentation character; the corresponding state space of $A$ is the set of unitization states whose restriction has norm one, not all states other than the augmentation character.

For every nonzero positive $a\in A$ there is a pure state $\phi$ with $\phi(a)=\|a\|$. Hence every nonzero closed two-sided ideal $J\subseteq A$ is omitted by the kernel of some irreducible GNS representation; that kernel is a primitive ideal, meaning the kernel of an irreducible representation.
items.strategy: Construct the GNS space from the positive-functional null left ideal, prove left multiplication contractive, and complete. In the nonunital case establish positivity and state normalization of the unique unitization extension, identify its GNS space with the completion of A/L_phi via an approximate unit, and prove the restricted representation cyclic and nondegenerate. Match cyclic vectors for uniqueness and use a dense subset for separability. Realize every positive subfunctional by a bounded positive form and Riesz operator in the commutant, prove the converse and order equivalence, and connect purity to irreducibility through norm-additivity, reducing projections, and Schur's lemma. Banach-Alaoglu gives compactness for every unital state space; a countable dense test family gives metrizability when the algebra is separable. Midpoint images of separated state pairs show nonextreme states form an F_sigma, so pure states are G_delta and Polish. Prove the nonunital state and pure-state correspondences, including purity of the augmentation. Hahn-Banach extends a maximal-spectrum state to a positive norming state, and Krein-Milman gives a pure norming state; applying this to x*x detects every nonzero closed ideal.

items.title: Mackey Borel structure and countable separation of the unitary dual
items.statement: Assume AC. Let G be a second-countable locally compact Hausdorff group, and let H-hat be its unitary dual. For each finite or countably infinite cardinal n fix a Hilbert carrier H_n of dimension n, where dimension means the cardinality of a complete orthonormal basis. Give the irreducible strongly continuous representations on H_n weak uniform convergence on compact subsets. On their disjoint union with the sum topology, quotient the Borel sigma-algebra by unitary equivalence to define the Mackey Borel structure on H-hat. Every irreducible representation has a separable carrier by the local proof, so the quotient map is onto. A Borel space is countably separated when a countable family of Borel sets separates every pair of distinct points. No standard-Borel or pure-state-quotient identification is asserted.
items.strategy: Prove every irreducible representation of a second-countable group has separable carrier: a nonzero vector has dense linear orbit span, a countable dense subset of the group gives a countable dense orbit, and finite Q+iQ combinations are countable and dense. AC and its countable-choice consequence provide the separability, countability, and Hilbert Fourier inputs. Transport each individual irreducible to a fixed finite or countable carrier by orthonormal-basis Fourier maps, proving the quotient map is onto. Inverse images preserve complements and countable unions, so the quotient construction is a sigma-algebra; state the countable-separation definition without asserting the property.

items.title: A measurable direct integral of unitary representations is strongly continuous
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $G$ be a second-countable locally compact Hausdorff group, let $(X,\mathcal B,\mu)$ be a sigma-finite standard-Borel measure space, let $(H_x,e_n(x))_{x\in X}$ be a measurable complex Hilbert field with countable fundamental family and direct integral $\mathcal H=\int_X^\oplus H_x\,d\mu(x)$, and let $(\pi_x)_{x\in X}$ be a measurable field of strongly continuous unitary representations of $G$ in the sense of [[def-direct-integral-of-unitary-representations]], with direct integral $\pi=\int_X^\oplus\pi_x\,d\mu(x)$. Then $g\mapsto\pi(g)$ is strongly continuous: whenever $g_k\to g$ in $G$, $\pi(g_k)\to\pi(g)$ in the strong operator topology. Equivalently, $\pi$ is a strongly continuous unitary representation of $G$ on $\mathcal H$ ([[def-strongly-continuous-unitary-representation]]).
items.strategy: This proves the strong-continuity sentence that the source states only as a citation to Dixmier's direct-integral theory ([Dixm-C*, Proposition 18.7.4]); the argument below is complete and quotes nothing unread. Fix $\xi\in\mathcal H$, viewed as a square-integrable measurable section, and a sequence $g_k\to g$ in $G$; second countability makes $G$ metrizable, so sequential continuity of $g\mapsto\pi(g)$ suffices. Every fibre is strongly continuous by hypothesis, so $\|\pi_x(g_k)\xi_x-\pi_x(g)\xi_x\|\to0$ for every $x$, and $$\|(\pi(g_k)-\pi(g))\xi\|^2=\int_X\|\pi_x(g_k)\xi_x-\pi_x(g)\xi_x\|^2\,d\mu(x).$$ For each fixed $k$ the integrand is measurable in $x$: the fields $x\mapsto\pi_x(g_k)$ and $x\mapsto\pi_x(g)$ are weakly measurable and $\xi$ is a measurable section, so all pointwise inner products involved are measurable ([[def-measurable-and-decomposable-operator-fields]], [[lem-measurable-sections-have-measurable-pointwise-inner-products]]). The integrand is dominated by $4\|\xi_x\|^2$, an integrable function independent of $k$, and it tends to $0$ pointwise, so the dominated convergence theorem gives $\|(\pi(g_k)-\pi(g))\xi\|\to0$. As $\xi$ was arbitrary, $\pi(g_k)\to\pi(g)$ strongly. Only the AC inherited from the direct-integral and measure-theory suppliers is used; the argument selects nothing.

items.title: Conull Borel uniformizations and Borel versions of measured suprema
items.statement:
Assume AC. Let $(X,\mathcal B,\mu)$ be a sigma-finite standard-Borel measure space and let $Y$ be a standard Borel space. If $R\subseteq X\times Y$ is Borel and every vertical section $R_x:=\{y\in Y:(x,y)\in R\}$ is nonempty, then there is a Borel conull set $X_0\subseteq X$ and a Borel map $s:X_0\to Y$ such that $(x,s(x))\in R$ for every $x\in X_0$. For any such $R$ and any bounded real-valued Borel function $\varphi:X\times Y\to\mathbb R$, define
$$m_{R,\varphi}(x):=\sup\{\varphi(x,y):y\in R_x\}.$$
For every rational $q$, the strict superlevel set $\{x:m_{R,\varphi}(x)>q\}$ is measurable in the completion of $\mu$, and there are a Borel function $\widetilde m:X\to\mathbb R$ and a Borel null set $N$ such that $\widetilde m=m_{R,\varphi}$ on $X\setminus N$. For any countable family of relations and scalar functions of these forms on the same measured base, the selectors and Borel versions may be restricted to one common Borel conull subset of $X$. A selector on every point of the original $X$ is not asserted.

items.title: Type I factor representations and type I groups
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $H$ be a nonzero separable complex Hilbert space and let $M\subseteq\mathcal B(H)$ be a concrete factor von Neumann algebra ([[def-factor-representation-and-primary-representation]]). A nonzero projection $p\in M$ is **minimal**, or **abelian**, when $pMp=\mathbb Cp$. The factor $M$ is of **type I** when it contains a nonzero minimal projection. A strongly continuous unitary representation $\pi$ of a topological group $G$ on a nonzero separable Hilbert space is a **type I factor representation** when its generated von Neumann algebra $\pi(G)''$ is a factor of type I; and a factor representation is of type I when it is a multiple of an irreducible representation (equivalently, by [[lem-separable-type-i-factors-are-multiples-of-irreducible-representations]], when $\pi(G)''$ contains a nonzero minimal projection). The group $G$ is **type I** when every factor representation of $G$ on a separable Hilbert space is of type I. The two descriptions of a type I factor representation agree: for a strongly continuous unitary representation $\pi$ on nonzero separable $H$ with $M=\pi(G)''$ a factor, $M$ contains a nonzero minimal projection if and only if there is an irreducible representation $\sigma$ of $G$ and $m\in\{1,2,\dots,\infty\}$ with $\pi\cong\sigma^{\oplus m}$ ([[lem-separable-type-i-factors-are-multiples-of-irreducible-representations]]).
items.strategy: Definition item. It records the minimal-projection criterion for type-I factors and the type-I group convention on separable factor representations. items.title: Polar decomposition inside a von Neumann algebra and nonzero partial isometries between nonzero projections in a factor
items.statement:
Assume AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $H$ be a complex Hilbert space and
$M\subseteq\mathcal B(H)$ a concrete von Neumann algebra
([[def-von-neumann-algebra-and-commutant]]). If $H=\{0\}$, part 1 is the
trivial zero-operator decomposition and part 2 has no nonzero projection inputs;
assume $H\ne\{0\}$ for the remaining clauses. A projection means a self-adjoint
idempotent in $M$; for projections $r,p$, $r\le p$ means $rp=pr=r$.
Projections $r,s\in M$ are called equivalent when there is a partial isometry
$w\in M$ with $w^*w=r$ and $ww^*=s$. Write $pMq:=\{pmq:m\in M\}$. Then:

1. Every $x\in M$ has a polar decomposition $x=v|x|$, where
   $|x|:=(x^*x)^{1/2}\in M$ and $v\in M$ is a partial isometry
   ([[def-isometry-coisometry-and-partial-isometry]]) with $v^*v$ the
   orthogonal projection onto $(\ker x)^\perp$ and $vv^*$ the orthogonal
   projection onto $\overline{\operatorname{ran}x}$.
2. If $M$ is a factor, meaning $M\cap M'=\mathbb C I$, and $p,q\in M$ are
   nonzero projections, then $pMq\ne\{0\}$. In particular, a nonzero partial
   isometry $v\in M$ exists with $v^*v\le p$ and $vv^*\le q$; equivalently,
   a nonzero subprojection of $p$ is equivalent to a nonzero subprojection of
   $q$.
items.strategy: For x∈M, prove x*x positive, obtain its positive root through continuous functional calculus, and place that root in M because its generated C*-algebra lies in the SOT-closed algebra M; the root gives ker|x|=ker x. Define the polar isometry on ran|x|, extend to its closure, and set it to zero on ker x; verify its initial and final projections locally. The regularizers x(|x|+1/n I)^−1 converge strongly to this partial isometry, so SOT closure puts it in M. For the factor clause, L=cl span MqH is nonzero and reducing for M and M′, so its projection lies in M∩M′ and equals I. If pMq=0 then p annihilates L=H, a contradiction. Swap p,q and polar-decompose a nonzero element of qMp to obtain the stated equivalent nonzero subprojections; no family-wide choice is used.

items.title: The full group C star algebra of a second-countable group is separable
items.statement:
Assume AC. Let $G$ be a second-countable locally compact Hausdorff group, let
$q:L^1(G)\to C^*(G)$ be the canonical map, and let
$\mathbb Q(i)=\{a+ib:a,b\in\mathbb Q\}$. Then $C^*(G)$ is separable. More
precisely, there are a countable dense set $S\subseteq L^1(G)$ and a countable
set $D\subseteq C^*(G)$ such that $q(S)\subseteq D$, $D$ is closed under
addition, multiplication, adjunction, and multiplication by elements of
$\mathbb Q(i)$, and the $\mathbb Q(i)$-linear span of $D$ is norm-dense in
$C^*(G)$.
items.strategy: Take the proved countable dense L1 family and use the full-norm bound to obtain dense canonical images. The countable alphabet S times the two adjoint flags has countably many finite words by finite powers and countable unions under AC implies Countable Choice. A second finite-list construction with rational-complex coefficients gives a countable dense star-subalgebra, with the stated closure properties checked locally.

items.title: A sequential approximate identity concentrated near the identity
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $G$ be a second-countable locally compact
Hausdorff group with a fixed left Haar measure $\mu$. There is a sequence
$(u_n)_{n\in\mathbb N}\subseteq C_c(G)$ such that $u_n\ge0$, $\int_Gu_n\,d\mu=1$,
and for every identity neighbourhood $U$ there is $n_0$ with
$\operatorname{supp}u_n\subseteq U$ for every $n\ge n_0$. It is a two-sided
approximate identity in $L^1(G)$:
$$\|f*u_n-f\|_1\longrightarrow0\quad\hbox{and}\quad\|u_n*f-f\|_1\longrightarrow0\qquad(f\in L^1(G)).$$
If $q:L^1(G)\to C^*(G)$ is the canonical dense-image map and $\rho$ is any
nondegenerate star-representation of $C^*(G)$ on a Hilbert space $H$, then
$$\rho(q(u_n))\longrightarrow I_H\quad\hbox{in the strong operator topology}.$$
We write $\rho(u_n)$ for $\rho(q(u_n))$ when the canonical map is understood.
The sequential construction and the representation limit are proved locally;
the cited literature passages supply only the stated C*-algebraic context.
items.strategy: A local countability lemma lists the second-countable basis members containing the identity without choice, giving a decreasing cofinal neighbourhood sequence. Restrict the supplied normalized, support-concentrated $L^1$ approximate-identity net to that sequence; its directed convergence gives both $L^1$ limits. Since $C_c(G)$ is dense in $L^1(G)$ and the canonical map is continuous with dense image, $q(C_c(G))$ is dense in $C^*(G)$. Boundedness of the nondegenerate representation carries this density to a dense span of representation vectors. Multiplicativity reduces convergence on those vectors to the left $L^1$ limit; a uniform representation bound extends it to every vector.

items.title: Matrix-coefficient properties of the transversal model of a monomial representation
items.statement: Assume AC. Let G be a topological group; for i=1,2 let H_i≤G be open subgroups, χ_i unitary characters, and T_i right transversals for H_i\G containing e. Let π_i be the transversal representations on ℓ²(T_i). For a bounded intertwiner S:ℓ²(T_1)→ℓ²(T_2), put f=Sδ_e. Then f=0 iff S=0. If π_1=π_2 on one carrier, f is a scalar multiple of δ_e iff S is scalar. For every t∈T_2 and h∈H_1, χ_2(α_2(t,h))f(t·_2h)=χ_1(h)f(t). If t has infinite H_1-orbit then f(t)=0. If f(t)≠0 and t·_2h=t, then tht^{-1}∈H_2 and χ_1(h)=χ_2(tht^{-1}).
items.strategy: The preceding transversal definition gives the cyclic vector δ_e and the action/cocycle formula. If Sδ_e=0, intertwining makes S zero on the dense cyclic orbit; if the representations coincide and Sδ_e is scalar δ_e, the same argument makes S scalar. For h∈H_1, π_1(h)δ_e=χ_1(h)δ_e, so evaluating Sπ_1(h)δ_e=π_2(h)Sδ_e at t gives the coefficient identity. Its modulus is constant on each H_1-orbit. On an infinite orbit, an arbitrarily large finite subset would contribute n|f(t)|² to the ℓ² square sum, contradicting its finite norm. At a fixed coset with f(t)≠0, cancel f(t) in the coefficient identity and use th=α_2(t,h)t to obtain the stabilizer and character conclusions. items.title: The two cyclic basis factors of the rank-two free group are self-commensurating with trivial cross-conjugate intersections
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $F=\langle a,b\rangle$ be the free group on
$a,b$, given the discrete topology, and let $A=\langle a\rangle$ and
$B=\langle b\rangle$. Then $F=A*B$ is the free product of two infinite cyclic
groups,
$\operatorname{Comm}_F(A)=A$ and $\operatorname{Comm}_F(B)=B$, and for every
$g\in F$,
$$g^{-1}Bg\cap A=\{e\}\quad\text{and}\quad g^{-1}Ag\cap B=\{e\}.$$
items.strategy: Use the free-product normal form after identifying F with the free product of the infinite cyclic subgroups generated by a and b. Prove same-factor malnormality by retaining end B- or A-syllables under conjugation, and prove cross-factor intersections by universal-property retractions. Trivial intersections with an infinite cyclic subgroup have infinite index. Verify explicitly that the discrete topology makes F a topological group and A,B open before applying the commensurator definition.

items.title: Two common diagonalizations differ by a bimeasurable base isomorphism and a measurable field of unitaries
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $(X,\mathcal B_X,\mu)$ and $(Y,\mathcal B_Y,
u)$ be sigma-finite standard-Borel measure spaces, let $(H_x)$ and $(K_y)$ be measurable complex Hilbert fields with countable fundamental families and all fibres nonzero, and put
$$\mathcal H=\int_X^\oplus H_x\,d\mu(x),\qquad \mathcal K=\int_Y^\oplus K_y\,d
u(y).$$
Let $\mathcal D_X$ and $\mathcal D_Y$ be the respective algebras of scalar multiplication operators. If a unitary $W:\mathcal H	o\mathcal K$ satisfies $W\mathcal D_XW^{-1}=\mathcal D_Y$, then there are conull Borel sets $X_0\subseteq X$, $Y_0\subseteq Y$, a bimeasurable bijection $c:X_0	o Y_0$, and a measurable field of unitaries $u_x:H_x	o K_{c(x)}$ such that $\lambda:=c_*(\mu|_{X_0})$ is equivalent to $
u|_{Y_0}$. If $r=d\lambda/d(
u|_{Y_0})$ and $J:\int_{Y_0}^\oplus K_y\,d\lambda(y)	o\int_{Y_0}^\oplus K_y\,d
u(y)$ is the square-root Radon–Nikodym unitary $(J\eta)(y)=\sqrt{r(y)}\,\eta(y)$, then
$$ igl(J^{-1}W\xi igr)_{c(x)}=u_x\xi_x\qquad	ext{for }\mu	ext{-almost every }x\in X_0.$$
The diagonal-model identity is preserved, $WI_{\mathcal H}W^{-1}=I_{\mathcal K}$, and the implementing base map and fibre field are unique up to null-set modification.

Normalize the equivalent measure class with the square-root Radon–Nikodym multiplier, transport one field to the common base, and apply the decomposable-commutant theorem to a block unitary to obtain the fibre unitaries. Prove uniqueness by countable separation and fibre-field uniqueness; handle empty or zero-measure direct integrals explicitly.

items.title: Bounded density and finite-vector transitivity for C*-representations
items.statement:
Assume AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $H$ be a complex Hilbert space and let
$D\subseteq\mathcal B(H)$ be a nondegenerate concrete C*-algebra
([[def-hilbert-space]], [[def-space-of-bounded-linear-operators]],
[[def-c-star-algebra]], [[def-nondegenerate-star-representation-of-a-banach-star-algebra]]).
Set $M:=D''$ in the commutant convention of [[def-von-neumann-algebra-and-commutant]]. If $H=\{0\}$, the operator-density and transitivity clauses below
are trivial; assume $H\ne\{0\}$ for those clauses. Then:

1. $D_{\mathrm{sa}}$ is strongly dense in $M_{\mathrm{sa}}$, and the unit ball
   of $D$ is strongly dense in the unit ball of $M$.
2. If $M=\mathcal B(H)$, then every finite self-adjoint vector prescription
   compatible with a self-adjoint operator is realized exactly: for
   $\xi_1,\ldots,\xi_n\in H$ and $c=c^*\in\mathcal B(H)$, there is
   $a=a^*\in D$ with $a\xi_j=c\xi_j$ for all $j$. Separately, if the prescribed vectors are finitely many orthonormal
   eigenvectors of $c$ with eigenvalues in a closed interval
   $J\subseteq\mathbb R$ containing $0$, an $a\in D_{\mathrm{sa}}$ can be
   chosen with spectrum in $J$ and the same eigenvalues on those vectors.
   This spectrum-constrained variant makes no promise about additional
   arbitrary vector prescriptions after clipping.
3. If $M=\mathcal B(H)$, then for any unit vectors $\xi,\eta\in H$ there is a unitary $u$ in the
   minimal unitization $D^\sim$ ([[thm-minimal-c-star-unitization]]) whose
   represented operator sends $\xi$ to $z\eta$ for some $z\in\mathbb C$ with
   $|z|=1$. Here unitary has the usual C*-algebra meaning
   ([[def-self-adjoint-positive-unitary-and-normal-elements-of-a-c-star-algebra]]),
   and $D^\sim=D$ when $D$ is unital and $D+\mathbb C I$ otherwise.

For a complex C*-algebra $A$, two pure states $\phi,\psi$ are called unitarily
equivalent here when $\psi=\phi\circ\operatorname{Ad}(u)$ for some unitary
$u\in U(A^\sim)$, where $\operatorname{Ad}(u)(a)=uau^*$ and $A^\sim=A$ when
$A$ is unital and its minimal unitization otherwise
([[thm-minimal-c-star-unitization]], [[def-self-adjoint-positive-unitary-and-normal-elements-of-a-c-star-algebra]]). Their GNS
representations are irreducible exactly when the states are pure
([[lem-c-star-state-gns-purity-and-polish-state-space]],
[[def-state-on-a-c-star-algebra]]). If their GNS representations are
inequivalent, then $\|\phi-\psi\|=2$. Orthogonal unit vectors in one
irreducible carrier likewise give vector states at distance $2$. Consequently,
if $\|\phi-\psi\|<2$, then $\phi$ and $\psi$ are unitarily equivalent.
items.strategy:
Use a positive contractive approximate unit and nondegeneracy to obtain strong convergence to the identity. Unitalize D and apply the finite-tuple bicommutant argument for strong density; symmetrize and use real Hahn–Banach on the finite-tuple image for self-adjoint density. Prove SOT continuity of C0(R) calculus through resolvents and Stone–Weierstrass, with vectorwise spectral-tail bounds; clipping gives the self-adjoint unit-ball result. Amplify locally to the block C*-algebra M2(D), prove its nondegeneracy and bicommutant M2(M), and compress to obtain full unit-ball density.

For exact finite-vector transitivity, project onto the closed finite-dimensional span, use its orthonormal basis, and extend the self-adjoint target by b=prp+(I−p)rp+pr(I−p), with norm at most 3||rp||. Explicit residuals are recursively corrected with geometrically shrinking errors; Dependent Choice selects the correction sequence and the norm-convergent self-adjoint sum gives exact action. Clip the result to a closed interval while fixing the specified eigenvalues.

For inequivalent pure GNS representations, prove the direct-sum image is nondegenerate and its commutant has scalar diagonal blocks and zero intertwiners. Bounded density separates the cyclic vector expectations by two, after passing to a self-adjoint quotient representative. The same transitivity gives norm distance two for orthogonal vector states. Below distance two, identify the GNS carriers, construct an internal unitary vector transport, lift its self-adjoint generator through the closed C*-image, and exponentiate in the minimal unitization.

items.title: A separable type I factor is a multiple of an irreducible representation
items.statement: Assume AC. Let $M$ be a concrete type-I factor on a nonzero separable complex Hilbert space $H$. There is a finite or countably infinite exhaustive orthogonal family $(p_i)$ of minimal projections in $M$, equivalent to a fixed $p=p_{i_0}$, and partial isometries $t_i$ in $M$ with $t_i^*t_i=p$ and $t_it_i^*=p_i$. Put $E=\ell^2(I)$, $L=pH$. The unitary $W:E\otimes L\to H$, $W(\delta_i\otimes\eta)=t_i\eta$, satisfies $W^*MW=B(E)\otimes I_L$ and $W^*M'W=I_E\otimes B(L)$. If $\pi$ is a strongly continuous unitary representation of a topological group $G$ on $H$ and $\pi(G)''=M$, there is a strongly continuous irreducible representation $\sigma$ on $E$ with $W^*\pi(g)W=\sigma(g)\otimes I_L$, so $\pi$ is $\dim(L)$ copies of $\sigma$. Equivalently $N=M'$ is type I; a minimal $q$ in $N$ has invariant irreducible carrier $K=qH$, and an exhaustive orthogonal family $(q_i)$ of equivalent minimal projections in $N$ with $u_i^*u_i=q_i$ and $u_iu_i^*=q$ gives a unitary $V:H\to K^{\oplus m}$, $V\xi=(u_i\xi)$, $m=\text{number of }q_i$, intertwining $\pi$ with $m$ copies of $\pi|K$. The space $pH$ for a minimal $p$ in $M$ is the multiplicity space, not the irreducible carrier. In the direct-sum realization used here, the operators $\rho(A)(\eta_i)_{i\in I}:=(\sum_{j\in I}A_{ij}\eta_j)_{i\in I}$ for $A=(A_{ij})\in B(E)$ constitute the algebra written $B(E)\otimes I_L$, and $(I\star S)(\eta_i)_{i\in I}:=(S\eta_i)_{i\in I}$ for $S\in B(L)$ constitutes $I_E\otimes B(L)$.

items.title: Mackey-Shoda irreducibility criterion for monomial representations
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $G$ be a topological group, $H\le G$ an open subgroup and $\chi$ a unitary character of $H$. Assume that for every $g\in\operatorname{Comm}_G(H)\setminus H$ the restrictions of $\chi$ and of $\chi^g$ to the subgroup $H\cap g^{-1}Hg$ do not coincide, where $\chi^g(h):=\chi(ghg^{-1})$. Then $\operatorname{Ind}_H^G\chi$ is irreducible. In particular, if $H$ is open and $\operatorname{Comm}_G(H)=H$, then $\operatorname{Ind}_H^G\chi$ is irreducible for every unitary character $\chi$ of $H$; and if $N$ is an open normal subgroup and $\chi$ a unitary character of $N$, then $\operatorname{Ind}_N^G\chi$ is irreducible if and only if $\chi^g\neq\chi$ for every $g\in G\setminus N$.
items.strategy: By contraposition, as in Theorem 1.F.11 of the source. If $\pi=\operatorname{Ind}_H^G\chi$ is reducible there is a non-scalar intertwiner $S\in\operatorname{Hom}_G(\pi,\pi)$; by part (2) of [[lem-monomial-induced-representations-transversal-model-properties]] the vector $f=S\delta_e$ is not supported in $\{e\}$, while by part (4) its support is contained in the set of $t\in T$ with finite $H$-orbit. Pick $t\in T\setminus\{e\}$ with finite $H$-orbit and $f(t)\neq0$; then $t\in\operatorname{Comm}_G(H)\setminus H$. The adjoint computation $f'(t^*)=\chi(\alpha(t^*,t))f(t)$ for $t^*=e\cdot t^{-1}$ shows that $f'=S^*\delta_e$ is nonzero at $t^*$, so $t^*$ has finite $H$-orbit as well; applying part (5) with $t=t^*$ and $h$ in the stabiliser yields $\chi(h)=\chi(tht^{-1})$, i.e. $\chi$ and $\chi^t$ coincide on $H\cap t^{-1}Ht$, contradicting the hypothesis. The 'in particular' clauses are the specialisations $\operatorname{Comm}_G(H)=H$ (vacuous hypothesis) and the normal case, where the necessity direction is the same argument with the stabiliser described by conjugation.

items.title: Mackey-Shoda non-equivalence criterion for monomial representations
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $G$ be a topological group, $H_1,H_2\le G$ open subgroups and $\chi_1,\chi_2$ unitary characters of $H_1,H_2$. Assume that for every $g\in G$ such that $g^{-1}H_2g\cap H_1$ has finite index in both $g^{-1}H_2g$ and $H_1$, the restrictions of $\chi_2^g$ and $\chi_1$ to $g^{-1}H_2g\cap H_1$ do not coincide. Then $\operatorname{Ind}_{H_1}^G\chi_1$ and $\operatorname{Ind}_{H_2}^G\chi_2$ are not equivalent. In particular, if $g^{-1}H_2g\cap H_1$ has infinite index in $H_1$ for every $g\in G$ (for instance if it is trivial and $H_1$ is infinite), then the two monomial representations are inequivalent whenever $H_1\neq H_2$ up to the stated intersection pattern.
items.strategy: This is Theorem 1.F.16 of the source, proved by contraposition in the transversal model and fully reproduced there: if $\pi_1\cong\pi_2$ there is a nonzero intertwiner $S$, and $f:=S\delta_e\in\ell^2(T_2)$ is nonzero on some $t$ with finite $H_1$-orbit (parts (1) and (4) of the model lemma). Setting $t^*=e\cdot_1t^{-1}$ and using the adjoint $S^*$ together with the coefficient formula of part (5) shows that $tH_1t^{-1}\cap H_2$ has finite index in $H_2$ and that $\chi_1$ and $\chi_2^t$ coincide on $t^{-1}H_2t\cap H_1$, contradicting the hypothesis. The 'in particular' clause is the vacuous case of the hypothesis when every such intersection has infinite index (a group of infinite index is not of finite index), which holds for the free-group example used on the examples page.

items.title: Disintegration of a separable group representation over a commuting diagonal algebra
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $G$ be a second-countable locally compact Hausdorff group, $(\pi,H)$ a separable strongly continuous unitary representation, $A\subseteq\pi(G)'$ an abelian concrete von Neumann algebra, $(X,\mathcal B,\mu)$ a sigma-finite standard-Borel space with a measurable Hilbert field $(H_x,e_n(x))$ and direct integral $\mathcal H=\int_X^\oplus H_x\,d\mu(x)$, and $U:H\to\mathcal H$ a unitary operator with $UAU^{-1}=\mathcal D$, the algebra of diagonalisable operators. Then there exist a measurable field $(\pi_x)_{x\in X}$ of strongly continuous unitary representations of $G$ on the fibres, defined for every $x$ by an arbitrary choice on a null set, such that for every $g\in G$ $$U\pi(g)U^{-1}=\int_X^\oplus\pi_x(g)\,d\mu(x),$$ and the field $x\mapsto\pi_x(G)''$ of von Neumann algebras generated by the fibres is a measurable field in the sense of [[def-measurable-field-of-von-neumann-algebras]]; moreover $\pi_x$ is nondegenerate for $\mu$-almost every $x$.
items.strategy: Transfer to the model: replacing $\pi$ by $U\pi U^{-1}$ we may assume $H=\mathcal H$, $A=\mathcal D$, hence $\pi(G)\subseteq\mathcal D'$ and every $\pi(a)$ $(a\in C^*(G))$ is decomposable, with a unique measurable essentially bounded fibre field $x\mapsto\rho_x(a)$ ([[thm-decomposable-operators-are-the-commutant-of-diagonal-multiplication]]). Choose a countable norm-dense rational-$*$ subalgebra $(a_k)$ of $C^*(G)$ (separable C*-algebra lemma). On the countable intersection of the conull sets on which the finitely many relations $T_{k+l}=T_k+T_l$ (rational scalars), $T_{kl}=T_kT_l$, $T_{k^*}=T_k^*$ hold, and on which $\|T_k(x)\Vert\le\|a_k\|$, the map $a_k\mapsto T_k(x)$ is a contractive $*$-homomorphism of a dense subalgebra; extend by norm continuity to a $*$-homomorphism $\rho_x:C^*(G)\to\mathcal B(H_x)$ with $\|\rho_x\Vert\le1$ (the extension is measurable in $x$ for each $a$, being a uniform limit of the measurable fields $x\mapsto\rho_x(a_k)$ along a sequence $a_k\to a$). Nondegeneracy almost everywhere: let $(u_n)$ be the sequential approximate identity of the previous lemma; the integrated operators satisfy $\rho(u_n)\to I$ strongly, and $\rho(u_n)=\int^\oplus\rho_x(u_n)\,d\mu$, so the fibre projections onto $\overline{\rho_x(C^*(G))H_x}$ converge strongly to $I$ in the integral and hence equal $I$ for almost every $x$ (dominated convergence for the squared norms against a countable fundamental family). Apply [[thm-nondegenerate-representations-of-c-star-g-are-unitary-representations-of-g]] fibrewise to obtain strongly continuous unitary representations $\pi_x$ of $G$ with $\rho_x(a)=\pi_x(a)$; measurability of $x\mapsto\pi_x(g)$ follows by writing $\pi_x(g)$ as the strong limit of $\rho_x(f_n)$ for a sequence $f_n\in L^1(G)$ forming an approximate identity at $g$ (matrix coefficients converge pointwise, hence the limit is measurable). Extend the field to all of $X$ by setting $\pi_x$ to be the trivial representation on $H_x$ off the conull set; the fibrewise identities hold everywhere by construction, so the definition of the direct integral applies and yields $U\pi(g)U^{-1}=\int^\oplus\pi_x(g)\,d\mu(x)$. The field of generated von Neumann algebras is generated by the measurable fields $x\mapsto\rho_x(a_k)$ almost everywhere, hence measurable. No operators are disintegrated separately over the uncountable index $G$, and no common null set over $G$ is used.

items.title: Measurable fields of von Neumann algebras have measurable commutants and centers
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $(M_x)_{x\in X}$ be a measurable field of unital von Neumann algebras on a measurable Hilbert field $(H_x)$ with countable fundamental family over a sigma-finite standard-Borel measure space $(X,\mathcal B,\mu)$, all fibres separable. Write $\mathcal M:=\int_X^\oplus M_x\,d\mu(x)$ for the direct integral. Then: (1) on a common conull Borel stratum there are WOT-dense countable measurable sections of the unit balls of $M_x$, $M_x'$ and $Z(M_x)$; in particular the commutant field $x\mapsto M_x'$ and the centre field $x\mapsto Z(M_x)=M_x\cap M_x'$ are measurable fields of von Neumann algebras; (2) $\mathcal M$ is a concrete von Neumann algebra on $\int_X^\oplus H_x\,d\mu(x)$; (3) $\mathcal M'=\int_X^\oplus M_x'\,d\mu(x)$; (4) $Z(\mathcal M)=\int_X^\oplus Z(M_x)\,d\mu(x)$; and if two measurable fields of unital von Neumann algebras have the same direct integral, then they coincide almost everywhere.

Select dense unit-ball sections, identify the global commutant by decomposability, take the double commutant, and prove centre/equality-of-fields identities from representative uniqueness.

items.title: Pure-state excision and density of faithful essential vector-state orbits
items.statement: Assume AC. For a pure state $\phi$ of a unital C*-algebra $A$ there is a net of positive norm-one contractions $b_t$ with $\phi(b_t)=1$ such that $\|b_t x b_t-\phi(x)b_t^2\|\to0$ for every $x\in A$. The sets $U_{a,\epsilon}=\{\psi\in S(A):\psi(a)>1-\epsilon\}$, where $a\ge0$, $\|a\|=\phi(a)=1$ and $\epsilon>0$, form a weak-star neighborhood basis at $\phi$. If $\pi$ is a faithful irreducible representation with $\pi(A)\cap\mathcal K(H)=\{0\}$, its pure vector states from unit vectors orthogonal to any prescribed finite-dimensional subspace of $H$ are weak-star dense in $P(A)$. For nonunital $A$ the same assertions hold with $a,b_t\in A$, using the unique state extension to the minimal unitization.

items.title: Faithful essential pure-state orbits obstruct countable separation
items.statement: Assume AC. Let $B$ be a separable primitive C*-algebra admitting a faithful irreducible representation with no nonzero compact operators in its image. Here a faithful pure state means one whose GNS representation is faithful. These states form a nonempty Polish $G_\delta$ subspace $F$ of $P(B)$. Every orbit under $U(\widetilde B)$ is dense, meager and $F_\sigma$ in $F$; every invariant Borel subset is meager or comeager. No countable invariant Borel family separates these orbits, and there are inequivalent faithful irreducible representations. Consequently, for any separable non-GCR C*-algebra $A$, its primitive-kernel map is not injective and its Mackey dual is not countably separated. For C*-algebras the Mackey structure means the quotient Borel structure of nondegenerate irreducible representations on fixed finite or countably infinite Hilbert carriers, with pointwise operator-matrix coordinates; the group version is [[def-mackey-borel-structure-and-countable-separation]].

The pure-state-to-GNS-kernel map is continuous and open onto $\operatorname{Prim}(A)$, and $\operatorname{Prim}(A)$ is Baire. A proper ideal is prime when two closed ideals with product contained in it cannot both strictly contain it; primitive means a kernel of an irreducible representation.

items.title: Irreducible class and multiplicity of a type I factor representation are well defined
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $G$ be a topological group, let $\sigma,\sigma'$ be irreducible strongly continuous unitary representations on nonzero separable Hilbert spaces $K,K'$, and let $m,m'\in\{1,2,\dots,\infty\}$. If $\sigma^{\oplus m}\cong(\sigma')^{\oplus m'}$, then $\sigma\cong\sigma'$ and $m=m'$. Consequently, if $\pi$ is a factor representation of $G$ whose generated von Neumann algebra is a type I factor, then the irreducible representation $\sigma$ and the multiplicity $m$ in any decomposition $\pi\cong\sigma^{\oplus m}$ are determined up to unitary equivalence by $\pi$ alone.
items.strategy: In the corrected amplification pi=sigma^{oplus m}, the commutant is B(l2(m)) tensor I_K: compute operator blocks and use Schur. An equivalence of two amplifications gives an isomorphism of these commutants. For finite m its complex algebra dimension is m^2, while the infinite case is infinite dimensional, so m=m'. A minimal projection in either commutant cuts out an invariant irreducible carrier, and any two minimal projections are equivalent within that commutant; the connecting partial isometry commutes with the representation and gives equivalent restrictions. Consequently sigma and sigma' have the same unitary class. This uses minimal projections in the commutant, not pH for minimal p in the generated algebra; that latter space is the multiplicity space.

items.title: Central disintegration: fibre commutant, centre and factoriality
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $G$ be a second-countable locally compact group, $(\pi,H)$ a separable strongly continuous unitary representation, and let $U:H\to\int_X^\oplus H_x\,d\mu(x)$ be a direct-integral model with diagonal algebra $\mathcal D$ such that $U Z(\pi(G)'')U^{-1}=\mathcal D$ (that is, $U$ diagonalises the centre). Put $M:=U\pi(G)''U^{-1}$. Then $\mathcal D\subseteq M\subseteq\mathcal D'$, and, for the measurable field of von Neumann algebras $x\mapsto M_x:=\pi_x(G)''$ generated by the disintegration $\pi=\int^\oplus\pi_x\,d\mu$ of [[lem-separable-group-c-star-representations-disintegrate-over-a-commuting-diagonal-algebra]], one has $$M=\int_X^\oplus M_x\,d\mu(x),\qquad M'=\int_X^\oplus M_x'\,d\mu(x),\qquad Z(M)=\int_X^\oplus Z(M_x)\,d\mu(x).$$ Consequently $Z(M_x)=\mathbb C I_{H_x}$ for almost every $x$, i.e. $\pi_x$ is a factor representation for almost every $x$; and if two measurable fields of unital von Neumann algebras have the same direct integral they agree almost everywhere, so the centre field is intrinsically determined.

items.title: Compact groups are type I and their direct integrals collapse to discrete Hilbert sums
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $K$ be a compact second-countable group. Every nonzero factor representation of $K$ on a separable complex Hilbert space is a multiple of one finite-dimensional irreducible representation; consequently $K$ is type I. Every strongly continuous unitary representation $(\pi,H)$ on a separable complex Hilbert space has the canonical isotypic decomposition
$$\pi\cong\bigoplus_{\alpha\in I}m_\alpha\pi_\alpha,\qquad m_\alpha\in\{1,2,\ldots,\infty\},$$
where $I\subseteq\widehat K$ is at most countable, the representatives $\pi_\alpha$ are finite dimensional, and $\infty$ denotes countably infinite multiplicity. The sum is the completed orthogonal Hilbert sum, with $I=\varnothing$ allowed when $H=0$. In the left regular representation the multiplicity of each irreducible is its dimension. Thus compact-group representations admit atomic direct-integral models; this concerns the canonical isotypic decomposition, not the atomicity of every redundant parameter measure.

items.title: Central decomposition into factor representations
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $G$ be a second-countable locally compact Hausdorff group and let $(\pi,H)$ be a strongly continuous unitary representation of $G$ on a separable Hilbert space $H\neq\{0\}$. Then there exist a sigma-finite standard-Borel measure space $(X,\mathcal B,\mu)$, a measurable Hilbert field $(H_x,e_n(x))$ with $H_x\neq\{0\}$ for $\mu$-almost every $x$, a measurable field $(\pi_x)$ of strongly continuous unitary representations of $G$ on the fibres, with $\pi_x$ a factor representation for almost every $x$, and a unitary $$U:H\longrightarrow\int_X^\oplus H_x\,d\mu(x)$$ such that (1) $U\pi(g)U^{-1}=\int_X^\oplus\pi_x(g)\,d\mu(x)$ for every $g\in G$; (2) $UZ(\pi(G)'')U^{-1}=\mathcal D$, the algebra of diagonalisable operators; (3) $U\pi(G)''U^{-1}=\int_X^\oplus\pi_x(G)''\,d\mu(x)$ and $U\pi(G)'U^{-1}=\int_X^\oplus\pi_x(G)'\,d\mu(x)$. Such a decomposition is called a **central decomposition** of $\pi$.
items.strategy: Let $M:=\pi(G)''$ and $Z:=Z(M)=M\cap M'$, an abelian concrete von Neumann algebra on the nonzero separable $H$. Choose a self-adjoint generator $S$ of $Z$ ([[lem-separable-abelian-von-neumann-algebras-have-a-self-adjoint-generator]]) and apply the spectral multiplicity model ([[thm-spectral-multiplicity-model-for-separable-abelian-von-neumann-algebras]]) to obtain a compact $K=\sigma(S)\subseteq\mathbb R$, a nonzero finite measure $\mu$, a multiplicity function $m\ge1$ and a unitary $U:H\to\int_K^\oplus\mathbb C^{m(t)}\,d\mu(t)$ carrying $Z$ onto the diagonal algebra. Applying the disintegration lemma to $A=Z\subseteq\pi(G)'$ yields the measurable field $(\pi_x)$ with $U\pi(g)U^{-1}=\int^\oplus\pi_x(g)\,d\mu(x)$ and $UMU^{-1}\subseteq\mathcal D'$, and the previous lemma (with $\mathcal D\subseteq UMU^{-1}$ because $Z\subseteq M$) gives $M=\int M_x$ and $Z(M_x)=\mathbb C I_{H_x}$ for almost every $x$. Hence each fibre is factorial. The multiplicity function of the spectral model satisfies $m\ge1$ by construction, so $H_x\neq0$ almost everywhere. All assertions are restricted to the standard, sigma-finite, separable hypotheses under which the spectral model and the disintegration lemma are proved.

items.title: Measurable splitting of a field of type I factors into irreducible representations with multiplicity
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $(M_x)_{x\in X}$ be a measurable field of type I factors on a measurable Hilbert field $(H_x,e_n(x))$ with all fibres separable and nonzero, over a sigma-finite standard-Borel measure space, and let $(\pi_x)$ be a measurable field of strongly continuous unitary representations of a second-countable group $G$ with $\pi_x(G)''=M_x$ for almost every $x$. Then, after deleting a null set, there exist (1) a measurable field of nonzero separable Hilbert spaces $(K_x)$; (2) a measurable function $m:X\to\{1,2,\dots,\infty\}$, the **multiplicity function**; (3) a measurable field $(\sigma_x)$ of irreducible strongly continuous unitary representations of $G$ on $K_x$; and (4) a measurable field of unitaries $V_x:H_x\to K_x^{\oplus m(x)}$ such that $$V_x\pi_x(g)V_x^{-1}=\sigma_x(g)^{\oplus m(x)}\qquad\text{for every }g\in G\text{ and almost every }x.$$ Moreover the pair $(\text{unitary class of }\sigma_x,\ m(x))$ is uniquely determined by $(\pi_x)$ up to null sets. In the single-fibre case this is exactly the statement that a separable type I factor representation is a multiple of an irreducible with well-defined multiplicity.

Use the complete local conull Borel uniformization and scalar-version lemma and the corrected dense-unit-ball commutant-field supplier. The following quantitative construction replaces greedy/Zorn field selection; it is a scaffold proof plan to be authored, not an acceptance certificate.

Pass to countably many constant-dimension strata and trivialize H_x measurably. Set N_x=M_x′; it is a measurable type-I factor field by the corrected single-fibre lemma and the commissioned commutant-field lemma. Its unit ball can be represented by countably many WOT-dense measurable sections. Use a measurable orthonormal fundamental frame (f_j), allowing f_j=0 beyond the fibre dimension, and put

phi_x(T) = sum_{j≥1} 2^{-j} <T f_j(x), f_j(x)>.

For positive T this is a finite faithful normal functional; its total value on I is at most 1, and positive on every nonzero projection. No normalization is needed. Matrix coefficients and bounded countable sums show it is jointly Borel on bounded operator fields.

On a fixed dimension stratum the set of pairs (x,q) with q a nonzero minimal projection in N_x is Borel. Spell this out: q=q*=q², q≠0; q commutes with the countable generators of M_x; and for every member a_j(x) of a WOT-dense countable family in (N_x)_1,

q a_j(x) q = [phi_x(q a_j(x) q)/phi_x(q)] q.

These countable equations characterize qN_xq=Cq: for fixed q, compression is WOT-continuous, and phi_x is WOT-continuous on bounded balls by the uniformly convergent coefficient series. All products are Borel on bounded operator balls (their matrix coefficients are limits of finite coordinate sums); WOT continuity of joint multiplication is neither required nor true. This graph is not presumed compact.

Construct residual r_0=I. At step n let s_n(x) be the supremum of phi_x(q) over minimal projections q in N_x with q≤r_{n-1}; set s_n=0 if r_{n-1}=0. Every nonzero residual in a type-I factor contains a minimal projection, so s_n>0 there. The sets {s_n>t} are projections of Borel sets, hence analytic. The local selection prerequisite must include their measurability in the completed sigma-finite base measure. Replace s_n by a Borel version outside a Borel null set. Select q_n with q_n≤r_{n-1} and phi_x(q_n)>s_n(x)/2; set q_n=0 on the zero-residual set. The conull Borel selector applies to this nonempty Borel relation. Put r_n=r_{n-1}-q_n. These operations are measurable. Iterate countably and discard the union of the exceptional Borel null sets once.

**Exhaustion proof.** At fixed x, suppose r_infty=strong-limit r_n is nonzero. It is a projection in N_x and contains a nonzero minimal q. Faithfulness gives c=phi_x(q)>0. Because q≤r_{n-1} at every step, s_n≥c, so phi_x(q_n)>c/2 for every n. Orthogonality implies sum_n phi_x(q_n)≤phi_x(I)≤1, contradiction. Thus sum_n q_n=I. This quantitative rule, unlike arbitrary greedy selection, forces exhaustion.

Select q_1 as above; it is nonzero everywhere on the retained nonzero-field base. Set K_x=q_1(x)H_x with fundamental sections q_1 f_j; this is a measurable Hilbert subfield. Let m(x) be the number of nonzero q_n(x), a value in {1,2,...,infinity}. Since the construction stops only at r=0 and keeps all later q_n zero, {m≥n}={q_n≠0}, a Borel set. This m is the multiplicity; dim K_x is the irreducible carrier dimension and can differ from m.

On {q_n≠0}, choose u_n(x) in N_x satisfying u_n* u_n=q_n and u_n u_n*=q_1. The solutions are nonempty by the factor/minimal-projection structure. Their graph is Borel by the same countable commutation and operator-product test. Apply the **general conull Borel selector**, not the compact selector; take u_1=q_1 and u_n=0 where q_n=0. Remove countably many null exceptional sets. No independent selection of all matrix units is needed: u_i* u_j gives the compatible units automatically.

Define sigma_x=pi_x|K_x and V_x xi=(u_n(x)xi) over n with q_n≠0. The single-fibre inverse formula proves V_x unitary and the amplification identity. Measurability of K, direct-sum field, V and V^{-1} follows from their countable fundamental matrix coefficients; sum expressions are pointwise norm limits. Restriction preserves strong continuity, and q_1N_xq_1=Cq_1 gives irreducibility. u(y)$, $\pi\cong\int^\oplus\sigma_y\,d
u$, in the sense of [[thm-central-decomposition-into-factor-representations]]. Then there exist conull Borel sets $X_0\subseteq X$, $Y_0\subseteq Y$, a bimeasurable bijection $c:X_0	o Y_0$ with $c_*(\mu|_{X_0})$ equivalent to $
u|_{Y_0}$, and a field of unitaries $u_x:H_x	o K_{c(x)}$ that is measurable over $X_0$ and satisfies $$u_x\pi_x(g)u_x^{-1}=\sigma_{c(x)}(g)\qquad	ext{for every }g\in G	ext{ and }\mu	ext{-almost every }x\in X_0.$$ Consequently the two central decompositions determine the same base modulo null sets and null-set modification, and the fibre representations are unitarily equivalent almost everywhere through a measurable field.

Applying this to a countable dense rational-$*$ family in $C^*(G)$ gives a common conull set for all generators, and strong continuity of the fibre representations together with density extends the identity to every $g\in G$ on that common conull set (the exceptional set depends only on the countable family, not on $G$). The measure-class statement follows from $c_*\mu\sim\nu$; composing with the square-root Radon-Nikodym unitary of [[lem-direct-integrals-transport-along-bimeasurable-base-isomorphisms]] if one wants the literal measure $c_*\mu$ rather than an equivalent one.

items.title: Irreducible direct integral decomposition for type I groups
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $G$ be a second-countable locally compact group of type I and let $(\pi,H)$ be a strongly continuous unitary representation on a separable Hilbert space. Then the central decomposition of $\pi$ refines to a direct integral over the unitary dual: there exist a standard measure $\mu$ on $\widehat G$, a measurable multiplicity function $m:\widehat G\to\{1,2,\dots,\infty\}$, a measurable field $(H_\sigma)$ of Hilbert spaces over $\widehat G$ and a unitary $U:H\to\int_{\widehat G}^\oplus H_\sigma\,d\mu(\sigma)$ such that for $\mu$-almost every $\sigma$, the fibre representation is equivalent to $m(\sigma)$ copies of $\sigma$ and $$U\pi(g)U^{-1}=\int_{\widehat G}^\oplus m(\sigma)\,\sigma(g)\,d\mu(\sigma)\qquad(g\in G),$$ where the integral is formed from the multiplicity field. Null-support fibres may be taken to be zero; no representative of every class of the entire dual is asserted. For H=0 take the zero measure and zero field.
items.strategy:
Handle H=0 first: the now-standard dual carries mu=0, set H_sigma=0 and m=1, and use the zero representation field; the fibre-labelled claim is mu-almost-everywhere and hence vacuous, while the integral is the zero Hilbert space. No factor decomposition of a zero representation is invoked. For H!=0 use the nonzero-carrier central decomposition below. After constructing the conull Borel dual support B, extend the Hilbert and representation fields by zero and multiplicity by1 on its null complement; the statement asserts the class identification only mu-almost-everywhere, consistent with the approved measure-theoretic claim and no global representative selection. Central decomposition and corrected measurable type-I splitting first give pi over X as sigma_x tensor I_{l2(m_x)}. Measurable Gram–Schmidt and the GNS/representation class coding make f(x)=[sigma_x] Borel into the now-standard dual. Normalize the sigma-finite scalar measure to an equivalent probability measure, keeping the same representation via the square-root Radon–Nikodym unitary. Its pushforward nu is a Borel probability on the standard dual, hence a standard measure.

   One must not silently assume that f is a base isomorphism or that its image is Borel. Its analytic image has full nu measure; local measured-projection/Borel-version arguments give a conull Borel subset B of that image. The existing conull Borel uniformization selects a representative x_b with f(x_b)=b, and sigma_b=sigma_{x_b} is a measurable field on B. On the original base select measurable unitaries intertwining sigma_x with sigma_{f(x)}: the relation is Borel using countably many integrated algebra generators, unitary equations and constant-dimension strata, and its fibres are nonempty by equality of classes. The field selector thus gives pi ≅ integral_X sigma_{f(x)} tensor I_{l2(m_x)}.

   Use the actual earlier scalar standard-Borel disintegration supplier `thm-disintegration-of-a-joint-law-on-standard-borel-spaces` for the joint law of (f(x),x). Its conditional kernels nu_b are supported on f^{-1}(b) almost everywhere: apply the conditional identities to a countable separating generating algebra of the dual, then remove the countable exceptional set. Put L_b=L2(X,nu_b;l2(m_x)). This is a measurable Hilbert field: a countable generating algebra of X, tensored with the coordinate indicator sections for m_x, gives a countable fundamental family whose Gram coefficients are conditional integrals and therefore Borel. Density follows from scalar simple-function approximation and finite-coordinate truncation. Conditional scalar Fubini on these elementary sections, followed by density, gives a unitary regrouping into integral_B sigma_b tensor I_{L_b}. This explicitly supplies the required Hilbert-field Fubini interface; it is not a citation replacing it. Its multiplicity dim(L_b) is Borel by the already proved dimension-strata construction.

   This regrouped representation is central. For each closed ideal J in C*(G), the support projection of pi(J)H is a central projection in M=pi(C*(G))'': it is the strong limit of an approximate identity of J and its range is reducing. On the b fibre it equals I iff J is not contained in ker(sigma_b), and zero otherwise. The countably many basic hull-kernel opens separate b and generate its Borel sigma-algebra, so these projections generate the full diagonal algebra D_B. Hence D_B⊆M⊆D_B'. The proved fibre-commutant/center supplier identifies M with its fibre integral and its center with D_B, since each fibre is a type-I factor. This proves the preserved dual disintegration with honest measure/multiplicity bookkeeping, without claiming a global selector for every point of the dual.
 Every equivalence is for the actual nondegenerate C*(G) representations and transfers to strongly continuous G representations through the earlier correspondence. This item contains no additional original citation exception; its proofs are local conditional on the criteria supplier.

items.title: Essential uniqueness of the type I irreducible disintegration
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $G$ be a second-countable locally compact group of type I and let $(\pi,H)$ be a strongly continuous unitary representation on a separable Hilbert space, with irreducible direct integral decompositions over $\widehat G$ as in [[thm-irreducible-direct-integral-decomposition-for-type-i-groups]], with measures $\mu,\nu$ and multiplicity functions $m,n$. Then $\mu$ and $\nu$ are equivalent measures on $\widehat G$ and $m=n$ almost everywhere; the decomposition is unique in this sense, and the pair $(\text{measure class},[m])$ is an invariant of $\pi$.

Both dual models are central by the ideal-support projection argument. The proved central-transport supplier gives a conull base isomorphism c and fibre factor unitaries. These preserve every ideal-support projection, since they intertwine the representation of the same algebra. Membership in each countable basic hull-kernel open therefore agrees for b and c(b). The base is standard and that family separates classes, so c(b)=b almost everywhere. Thus the two measures on the same dual are equivalent, and the corrected single-fibre multiplicity uniqueness gives identical multiplicities almost everywhere. This supplies the requested canonical measure-class/multiplicity claim rather than merely asserting uniqueness on arbitrary differently labelled bases.

items.title: The regular representation of the real line as a multiplicity-one integral of characters
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $G=\mathbb R$ with its usual additive locally compact topology and Borel Lebesgue Haar measure $m_{\mathbb R}$. Give the Pontryagin dual $\widehat{\mathbb R}$ its compact-open topology and a dual Haar measure $\mu$ normalized compatibly with Plancherel. For each $\chi\in\widehat{\mathbb R}$, set $H_\chi=\mathbb C$ and $\pi_\chi(t)z=\chi(t)z$. Then $(H_\chi)$ is the constant measurable Hilbert field over the standard-Borel, sigma-finite measure space $(\widehat{\mathbb R},\mu)$, and $(\pi_\chi)$ is a measurable field of strongly continuous one-dimensional unitary representations. Write $\mathcal F_-$ for the library's conjugate-phase Plancherel transform, whose $L^1\cap L^2$ formula is $\mathcal F_-f(\chi)=\int_{\mathbb R}f(t)\overline{\chi(t)}\,dm_{\mathbb R}(t)$, and define dual inversion by $(J\varphi)(\chi)=\varphi(\chi^{-1})$. Then $\mathcal F_+:=J\mathcal F_-$ is a unitary; on $L^1\cap L^2$ it has the positive-phase formula $\mathcal F_+f(\chi)=\int_{\mathbb R}f(t)\chi(t)\,dm_{\mathbb R}(t)$. Under the canonical identification $\int_{\widehat{\mathbb R}}^\oplus\mathbb C\,d\mu\cong L^2(\widehat{\mathbb R},\mu)$ it intertwines the left regular representation with the direct integral:
$$\lambda_{\mathbb R}\cong\int_{\widehat{\mathbb R}}^\oplus\pi_\chi\,d\mu(\chi).$$
The fibres have dimension one and the dual Haar measure has no point masses, giving the basic multiplicity-one continuous-spectrum model.
items.strategy: Identify the dual of the real line with R using the compact-open topology, giving a standard-Borel sigma-finite dual Haar base and a measurable constant C field. Apply the library Plancherel transform with conjugate phase; left translation multiplies by the inverse character. Dual inversion preserves Haar measure, so composing with inversion gives the positive-phase intertwiner with multiplication by chi(t). Identify the scalar L2 space with the direct integral and verify one-dimensional fibres and absence of point masses.

items.title: The left regular factor of an ICC discrete group is a non-type-I factor
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\Gamma$ be a countably infinite group in which every nonidentity conjugacy class is infinite (ICC), for instance the free group on two generators or the group of finitely supported permutations of $\mathbb N$. Let $\lambda_\Gamma$ be the left regular representation on $\ell^2(\Gamma)$ and $L(\Gamma):=W^*(\lambda_\Gamma(\Gamma))\subseteq\mathcal B(\ell^2(\Gamma))$. Then: (1) $\tau(T):=\langle T\delta_e,\delta_e\rangle$ is a faithful normal tracial state on $L(\Gamma)$ with $\tau(I)=1$, and $L(\Gamma)$ is infinite dimensional; (2) $L(\Gamma)$ is a factor, i.e. $Z(L(\Gamma))=\mathbb CI$; (3) $L(\Gamma)$ is not a type I factor, hence $\lambda_\Gamma$ is a factor representation that is not a multiple of an irreducible representation. Thus the canonical central decomposition of $\lambda_\Gamma$ has a single non-irreducible factor fibre, exhibiting that factor representations need not be irreducible and that the type I hypothesis in the irreducible disintegration theorem is essential.

items.title: Canonical compact-group decompositions are atomic Hilbert sums
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $K$ be a second-countable compact group with normalized Haar measure and let $(\pi,H)$ be a strongly continuous unitary representation on a separable complex Hilbert space. Its canonical isotypic decomposition is
$$\pi\cong\bigoplus_{\alpha\in I}m_\alpha\pi_\alpha,$$
with $I\subseteq\widehat K$ at most countable, $\pi_\alpha$ finite dimensional and $m_\alpha\in\{1,2,\ldots,\infty\}$. In fact $\widehat K$ is countable. Give it its discrete sigma-algebra and counting measure, and put $H_\alpha=\mathbb C^{m_\alpha}\otimes V_\alpha$ for occurring classes, where $\mathbb C^\infty$ means $\ell^2(\mathbb N)$, and $H_\alpha=0$ for the others. This measurable field realizes $\pi$ as the atomic direct integral of $m_\alpha\pi_\alpha$ over the full dual. Its Hilbert space is the completed square-summable orthogonal sum. For the left regular representation $m_\alpha=\dim V_\alpha$.

items.statement:

Then there are two direct integral decompositions into irreducible representations $$\lambda_F\cong\int_{\widehat A}^\oplus\operatorname{Ind}_A^F\chi\,d\mu(\chi)\cong\int_{\widehat B}^\oplus\operatorname{Ind}_B^F\psi\,d
u(\psi),$$ where $\mu,
u$ are Haar measures on the compact duals $\widehat A,\widehat B\cong\mathbb T$, every fibre $\operatorname{Ind}_A^F\chi$ and $\operatorname{Ind}_B^F\psi$ is irreducible, and $\operatorname{Ind}_A^F\chi

Moreover $F$ is not type I, because $L(F)$ is an infinite-dimensional non-type-I factor ([[ex-the-left-regular-factor-of-an-icc-discrete-group]]).
